transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

I came in because I was launching nonstop redesign projects at the plant, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting the shift plan myself—just taking on all of it. And then suddenly I couldn’t keep up with the plans I’d put in motion.
How long did this period of intense energy and nonstop project-launching last—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been going on for about three weeks, since I moved into the temporary apartment—the overdrive and then barely being able to function.
During those three weeks of high energy, did you find you needed much less sleep than usual—like only a few hours—while still feeling rested and full of energy?
Yeah. I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night and still getting to the plant feeling sharp and charged. It felt like sleep was optional—almost inefficient.
During those three weeks, did you feel unusually confident or special—like you had abilities, ideas, or importance well beyond your usual self?

Yeah. I honestly thought I could fix the entire production workflow faster than the consulting team could. When people raised concerns, I brushed them off—failure just didn’t seem possible to me then.
Before these past three weeks, have you ever had a similar period of high energy or, alternatively, a stretch of weeks where you felt unusually depressed, low, or hopeless?
Yes. Before this, I had a really heavy depressed stretch that lasted about three months. The move and getting assigned to the plant made it a lot harder to manage.

During those three weeks of high energy, did you experience anything like hearing voices or sounds others couldn't hear, or holding beliefs—like being chosen for a special mission or having powers—that others found unrealistic or tried to talk you out of?
No, I didn’t hear voices or anything like that. I felt very sure of myself, but I didn’t think I had powers or some special mission.
During those three weeks, did this high-energy period cause serious problems—like conflicts at work, risky decisions, or anything that led others to intervene or that required hospitalization?

Yes. I had to ask to be pulled out of a shift-planning meeting because I couldn’t manage it properly. Occupational health got involved too, since I wasn’t able to make the basic production decisions my job depends on.
